label: Hull SIH report daily
info: Writes Plan_OPT_EU, Time_Utilisation_EU and Daily_Losses_EU of site Hull (Data Source SIH) straight from the Insights Hub API, one file per production day. Read calls only. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] TRIGGERS & SITE SETTINGS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGERS AND SITE SETTINGS. Site Hull. Writes the three Tableau tables Plan_OPT_EU (machine x production day x shift x product), Time_Utilisation_EU (machine x day) and Daily_Losses_EU (one row per stop) straight from the Insights Hub API, one file per production day, with Data Source = SIH. The rows of a CONFIG line on source sih go to <root>/report (what Tableau reads), the others to <root>/candidate/sih. Schedule: a tick every hour; 1.1 goes on only in the local hour runHourLocal of the site in 1.1 CONFIG (the same local time in summer and winter; no hour: backfill only), then builds the production days that have ended and the days before them (REBUILD_DAYS). The production day starts at dayStartLocal o'clock local time (timeZone of the site), so it is 23, 24 or 25 hours long. Backfill: edit the inject payload {"start":"YYYY-MM-DD","end":"YYYY-MM-DD"} (production days) and click the button. 1.1 SITE SETTINGS is the only node to edit: site name, dry-run switch, rebuild days. The shared settings (credentials, root folder, lines, production-day start) come from the Config tab. dryRun is true by default. Then the site setup (Glidepaths, Machine Names, Shift Patterns from <root>/reference) and ONE MESSAGE PER DAY, one day every 5 s.

name: 1.1 SITE SETTINGS (edit here)
[2] SITE SETUP: GLIDEPATHS
info: STAGE 2 - the Glidepaths file of the site (<root>/reference/glidepaths/site=<Site>/, newest .csv) is listed, read and parsed, and the target lookup is stored in flow context: machine-site and month give the OEE, PDT and UPDT targets and the loss targets per sub group (the same node as the PBI report build). A missing file stops the run and the log says so.

name: 2.1 Set glidepaths folder
2.2 Pick the file
2.3 Build target lookup
[3] SITE SETUP: MACHINE NAMES
info: STAGE 3 - the Machine Names file of the site (<root>/reference/machine_names/site=<Site>/) gives Dept, Area and Product Type per MachineName (the report name of a CONFIG line). Unlike the PBI report build, the report filters of the site are not applied: the CONFIG lines choose the machines.

name: 3.1 Set machine names folder
3.2 Pick the file
3.3 Build machine lookup
[4] SITE SETUP: SHIFT PATTERNS
info: STAGE 4 - the Shift Patterns file (<root>/reference/shift_naming/site=All/) maps a raw shift name to the report shift; a SIH shift that already has a report name (Red, Green, Gold, Blue, Day, Night, Afternoon) is kept as it is. Then the day list: one message per production day, one every 5 s.

name: 4.1 Set shift folder
4.2 Pick the file
4.3 Build shift lookup
4.4 Start the day list
4.5 Build day list
4.6 Note status: day list built
[5] SETUP FAILED
info: STAGE 5 - a reference file that is missing or empty: one log line, nothing is built in this run.

name: 5.1 Describe failure
[6] DAY SETUP
info: STAGE 6 - one message per day: token request, OEE asset list, choose the assets, one message per asset (one per second). Function nodes cannot use fetch in the VFC, so every call is an http request node: the function before it sets msg.method, msg.url and msg.headers. A failure goes to the LOG and nothing is written for that day.

name: 6.1 Note status: DAY SETUP
6.2 Build token request
6.3 Build asset list request
6.4 Choose assets
[7] ASSET KPIs
info: STAGE 7 - one asset. 3.1 and 3.2: Asset Management GET asset (hierarchyPath), then evaluateKPIs POST (read-style, groupedByDateTime=true, recursive=false, no ORDER filter). 3.3 checks the response, 3.4 pivots it to one entry per hour. Every asset ends at the join, also when skipped or failed (link "to JOIN"), so the join never waits for a missing message.

name: 7.1 Build asset request
7.2 Build KPI request
7.3 Check day size
[8] KPI PARTS
info: STAGE 8 - the day evaluateKPIs call answered HTTP 413 (Request Entity Too Large: too many status changes for one call). The same KPIs are asked again hour by hour (one call per hour of the day window, one per second), a join waits for all hours and the answers are merged into one day answer (the hourly groups of every KPI, the same shape as the day call), which goes on to the check node of the day call. If an hourly call fails too, the day fails (no half days) and the log says "also on 1 h windows". The asset note in the log says "KPIs in n hourly parts".

name: 8.1 Build hour requests
8.2 Pack hour answer
8.3 Note status: KPI hourly parts
8.4 Merge hour answers
[9] KPI CHECK
info: STAGE 9 - the day answer of evaluateKPIs (from the day call or merged from the hourly parts) is checked, then pivoted to one entry per hour. A failed call ends at the join (link "to JOIN").

name: 9.1 Check KPI response
9.2 Pivot KPI results
[10] ASSET SHIFTS
info: STAGE 10 - one asset. The shift of an hour comes from the calendar of the asset. 4.1 asks the OEE config for the calendar id and the product collection id, 4.2 asks the calendar events that cover the production day, 4.3 turns them into shift rules (freq, interval, start, until, duration). A failed call or an asset without a calendar fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: 10.1 Build config request
10.2 Build calendar events request
10.3 Build shift rules
[11] ASSET PRODUCTS
info: STAGE 11 - one asset. 5.1 asks filterValues for the products and orders of the production day (the lists behind the Product and Order dropdowns of the OEE app). 5.2 checks the answer and asks the product list (name, code, description, design speed) of the product collection of the asset. A day without any product or order goes straight to "to ASSIGN"; an asset without a product collection goes on without master data ("to VALUES"). A failed call fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: 11.1 Build filter values request
11.2 Build product list request
[12] VALUE KPIs
info: STAGE 12 - one asset. 6.1 keeps the master data of the products of the day and sends ONE MESSAGE PER PRODUCT AND PER ORDER (4 per second: the VFC drops the messages of a day that runs too long, about 60 s, with no error; at 1 per second a shift day of 8 assets needed about 80 s). 6.2 builds the evaluateKPIs POST (read-style, hourly) filtered on that product or order. Every value message carries msg.parts of its asset group; the msg.parts of the asset (day join) waits in msg.assetParts. A failed call fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: 12.1 Build value messages
12.2 Build value KPI request
12.3 Check day size
[13] VALUE PARTS
info: STAGE 13 - the same hourly fallback for the evaluateKPIs call of one product or order that answered 413: hour by hour, joined, merged, then on to the collect node of the value calls. A separate lane from the day KPIs: one shared lane would make a loop.

name: 13.1 Build hour requests
13.2 Pack hour answer
13.3 Note status: VALUE hourly parts
13.4 Merge hour answers
[14] VALUE CHECK
info: STAGE 14 - the answer of one product or order call (from the call or merged from the hourly parts): 1 packs its hours with parts, the join waits for every value of the asset (no flow context: overlapping days lost updates there), 2 collects them and gives the asset its msg.parts back. A failed call fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: 14.1 Pack value hours
14.2 Collect value hours
[15] ASSIGN & PLAN
info: STAGE 15 - one asset. 7.1 gives every hour its product and order: the value that has parts in that hour; an hour without parts takes the value of the hour before it (the first hours take the next value). 7.2 groups the hourly KPIs per shift AND product and builds the pbi_plan_opt rows (total time = total minus shift plan stop, planned OpT = operational time, OEE time = used operational time, all in minutes; capacity = design speed per minute x planned OpT; downtime units = design speed per minute x downtime minutes; part name = product description, else name; product key = product code) and the pbi_time_utilisation row. An hour outside every shift gets shift_name null.

name: 15.1 Assign hours to products
15.2 Build plan rows
[16] ASSET STOPS
info: STAGE 16 - one asset. 8.1 downtimeReasons GET (size 5000, one page), 8.2 checks the response, 8.3 builds the pbi_daily_losses rows (one per stop that starts inside the production day: local date and time, shift, duration in minutes, loss group, sub group, equipment; product, part name and batch id (= order) of the hour of the stop; loss units = design speed per minute x duration), 8.4 builds the result of the asset and sends it to the join.

name: 16.1 Note status: ASSET STOPS
16.2 Build stops request
16.3 Check stops response
16.4 Build loss rows
16.5 Build asset result
[17] JOIN & BUILD TABLES
info: STAGE 17 - the join waits for all assets of the day. Collect the results, then turn them into the report columns: MachineName = the report name of the CONFIG line, Unique Machine Name = MachineName-Site, targets and loss targets from Glidepaths, Dept, Area, Product Type from Machine Names, shift kept or mapped, an empty sub group is Not Logged, an empty equipment Unclassed, Data Source = SIH; the rows are grouped by folder (line source sih: report, else candidate/sih). Decide writes NOTHING if any asset failed (no half days) and nothing in dry-run mode. Then one message per table and folder: output 1 = Plan_OPT_EU, 2 = Time_Utilisation_EU, 3 = Daily_Losses_EU, 4 = log.

name: 17.1 Note status: JOIN & BUILD TABLES
Wait for all assets of the day
17.2 Collect results
17.3 Build report columns
17.4 Decide day
17.5 Build table messages
[18] WRITE Plan_OPT_EU
info: STAGE 18 - parquet node, path and write object for Plan_OPT_EU (machine x production day x shift x product), one message per folder. The path is <folder>/Plan_OPT_EU/site=<Site>/Plan_OPT_EU_<production day>_sih.parquet, the same on every rerun, so a rerun replaces the day. The columns and types are those of the PBI report build (DATE as a day number, times of day on 1970-01-01).

name: 18.1 Set Plan_OPT_EU path
[19] WRITE Time_Utilisation_EU
info: STAGE 19 - parquet node, path and write object for Time_Utilisation_EU (machine x production day), one message per folder. The path is <folder>/Time_Utilisation_EU/site=<Site>/Time_Utilisation_EU_<production day>_sih.parquet, the same on every rerun, so a rerun replaces the day. The columns and types are those of the PBI report build (DATE as a day number, times of day on 1970-01-01).

name: 19.1 Set Time_Utilisation_EU path
[20] WRITE Daily_Losses_EU
info: STAGE 20 - parquet node, path and write object for Daily_Losses_EU (one row per stop), one message per folder. The path is <folder>/Daily_Losses_EU/site=<Site>/Daily_Losses_EU_<production day>_sih.parquet, the same on every rerun, so a rerun replaces the day. The columns and types are those of the PBI report build (DATE as a day number, times of day on 1970-01-01).

name: 20.1 Set Daily_Losses_EU path
[21] ERRORS
info: STAGE 21 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 21.1 Describe error
[22] LOG
info: STAGE 22 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 22.1 Format log line
22.2 Update run status
22.3 Build log write
[23] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 23 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.

name: 23.1 Append log rows
